concerns.text: FR-006 mandates a sensitivity analysis sweeping thresholds {0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40} to observe stability in the headline correlation coefficient. Task T043 attempts this but relies on `aligned_dataset.csv` (generated by T032) which is already biased by a single threshold match. There is no task to re-fetch raw stories and target datasets to perform a true independent sweep for each threshold, making the FR-006 requirement untestable as currently specified.

SC-002 requires validating matching precision against a stratified random sample of 100 manually annotated pairs to ensure a false-positive rate ≤ 5%. Task T025.2 only generates a local dataset of 50 pairs. There is no task to generate the required 100 pairs or to perform the specific precision calculation (false-positive rate) against this gold standard to verify the 0.9 precision threshold mentioned in US-2.

US-4 and SC-006 mandate that the primary dependent variable must be measured from human participants or a validated proxy. Tasks T009.6 (external fetch) and T009.6c (local pilot) exist, but there is no task to validate that the external dataset constitutes a 'validated proxy' or to ensure the local pilot meets the statistical power required for the primary analysis, risking a failure to satisfy the 'primary source' requirement.

SC-005 requires the analysis to run within GitHub Actions free-tier constraints (time/memory). While T007 enforces a minimum story count, there is no task to profile the runtime or memory usage of the full pipeline (T051) against the 45-minute/6GB limits defined in plan.md to ensure SC-005 is actually met before finalizing the report.

Task T009.6b references `data/raw/reader_responses_external.csv` or `reader_responses_local.csv` but does not explicitly handle the case where T009.6 fails and T009.6c is skipped, potentially leaving the pipeline without a source for the mapped CSV if both data collection paths fail.
